title: Programmed stage identity is selection evidence, not runtime activation

observed: The canonical queue requires deterministic hourly repertory coverage while preserving one continuity state and prohibits activation without stronger deployment evidence.

The latest Vercel queue update states that programmed-stage freshness requires exact commit binding, repertory digest binding, safety, continuity, production metadata, edition identity, and explicitly false runtime and deployment claims.

The same update records six passing focused tests but states that the full authenticated repertory suite was not executed and that deployment, audio-routing, and physical-device acceptance remain outstanding.
CURRENT_STATE continues to classify Vercel delivery as in_progress_blocked because immutable deployment verification is unavailable.
inferred: Language such as programmed, selected, scheduled, on stage, current production, or current edition can describe deterministic repertory resolution without proving browser execution, deployment, public reachability, audio playback, or physical-device behavior.
Continuity state and presentation state are related but non-identical: continuity is the preserved underlying identity; production identity is the currently selected outward form.
proposed: Attach claim_class=programmed_selection to repertory receipts and human summaries unless runtime activation is separately proven.
Reserve active, live, deployed, playing, audible, public, and running for claims backed by their corresponding immutable deployment or execution evidence.
When reporting the current production, include both the selected identity and an explicit runtime_claim=false boundary whenever activation evidence is absent.
superseded: The assumption that saying a production is on stage necessarily means it is executing on a deployed public surface.
The assumption that a passing selector or receipt test proves browser, network, audio, or physical-device behavior.
unresolved: Whether all existing repertory-facing summaries consistently distinguish programmed selection from activation.
Whether the complete authenticated repertory suite preserves this vocabulary boundary across every hourly production.
Whether older artifacts use active or live as shorthand for selection and therefore need additive clarification records.

proves: receipt-bound continuity and safety metadata when validated

minimum_evidence: immutable successful deployment identity bound to the exact tested commit
served-identity verification for the generated deployment hostname

falsification_route: Produce immutable exact-commit deployment and execution evidence demonstrating that a challenged use of active, live, playing, public, or running was correct; then add a superseding continuity record while retaining this boundary.
